verdicts.title: First Light dialog accepts a 999999-second exposure and has no upper bound, contradicting its own copy
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced exactly on display :89, profile v-widgets, with sim_camera_1 connected. Settings > Help & Tutorials > 'Capture your first light' > Start; selected the Exposure length field, Ctrl+A, typed 999999 (screenshot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-12.png shows the field holding 999999 with no error), clicked 'Start capture'. Native log /tmp/ns-audit/v-widgets/app.log line 90: '2026-08-02T16:04:41.808335Z INFO Starting 999999s exposure with gain=Some(100), offset=Some(50), bin=1x1'. Imaging then read 'Exposing... 999938.8s remaining' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-16-imaging.png) at 16:05:42 -- I recomputed it: 999999 - 60.2s elapsed = 999938.8, so the countdown is honest and an 11.57-day exposure really was committed. The cited location is correct: first_light_flow_dialog.dart:240-245 _parseExposure rejects only 'value == null || value <= 0', _start (247-262) has no other check, and the input formatter at 292-294 (FilteringTextInputFormatter.allow(RegExp(r'[0-9.]'))) imposes no length or magnitude limit. Nothing downstream clamps either: FirstLightOrchestrator.run (first_light_orchestrator.dart:233-240) also only rejects <= 0. SEVERITY CORRECTED P1 -> P2: this is a missing guard-rail, not a defect that fires on its own -- the field is pre-filled with a sane 5 and the app does exactly what it was told. Every bit of the 'costs a night' consequence is borrowed from the second finding (no way to cancel); with a working cancel this is a 5-second annoyance. The cheap upper-bound clamp is still the right fix, but a fixer should not be told this is the P1.

verdicts.title: Closing the First Light dialog mid-capture orphans the exposure, and there is no cancel inside the dialog
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced end to end, and I ran the control experiment the original finding did not. (1) Running state has no cancel: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-13-working.png shows 'Working on it... / Capturing exposure' with an indeterminate bar and only the title-bar X. Code agrees -- first_light_flow_dialog.dart:112-119, _actionsFor returns null for exposing/stretching/solving/annotating. (2) The X closes it mid-run: clicked the X at 16:05:2x, dialog gone (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-15-afterx.png), no new native log lines, and Imaging still read 'Exposing... 999938.8s remaining'. (3) The Imaging 'Abort capture' X is genuinely dead for this path, not merely silent -- this is the part I proved rather than assumed. I hovered it to confirm the target (tooltip beginning 'Abo', button highlighted, /tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-19-tooltip.png), clicked it twice; the counter ran on 999938.8 -> 999912.8 (999999 - 87.2s elapsed, recomputed) and the log gained ZERO lines. I then restarted the app, reconnected the camera, took a 120 s Snapshot FROM the Imaging screen and clicked the same X: the log immediately printed '2026-08-02T16:10:15.432291Z INFO Exposure cancelled'. So a working abort does log, and the first-light abort never reached the backend. Root cause is exactly where the finding points: imaging_screen_actions.dart:273 _abortCapture early-returns on 'if (!_isSingleCapture && !_isLooping) return;' -- imaging-screen-local flags a first-light capture never sets -- while imaging_preview_toolbar.dart:97 decides to SHOW the button from the global 'exposureProgress.remaining > 0'. Note the same guard means that button is offered and dead for any exposure the Imaging screen did not itself start (sequencer runs, centering); I did not drive those, so treat that as a code-level observation. (4) Camera stayed unusable: clicking Snapshot during the orphan produced no log line and no new exposure; only killing and restarting the process cleared it. PRECISION CORRECTION for the fixer: the finding implies the modal is freely dismissible, but it is not -- first_light_flow_dialog.dart:61 wraps it in PopScope(canPop: !state.isRunning) and I verified Escape is blocked mid-run (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/vw-14-esc.png, dialog still up). The single hole is the header close button: SkotiqDialog gates it on 'closeEnabled' (skotiq_dialog.dart:89, default true) and calls Navigator.pop directly (skotiq_dialog.dart:98-105), which PopScope does not intercept; FirstLightFlowDialog never passes closeEnabled. So the minimal fix is 'closeEnabled: !state.isRunning' plus a real cancel -- and a real cancel needs a cancel path that does not exist yet: FirstLightOrchestrator.run and firstLightControllerProvider have no cancel/abort token at all (only reset(), first_light_provider.dart:38, which clears UI state while the exposure keeps running). Severity P1 confirmed, not raised: the app-restart recovery keeps it out of P0, but a progress modal whose only exit does not cancel, backed by a device-abort button that lies, is the shape that costs a night.
